entries.title: The Top 10 Best e-Readers for Fall 2026
entries.summary: Want to buy a new e-reader in the next few months? The Good e-reader Top Picks breaks down the best devices from all of the major companies. The post The Top 10 Best e-Readers for Fall 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Fall is here, and it’s the perfect time to buy a new e-reader as the weather cools. Buying a new e-reader is highly compelling because the hardware market has shifted from minor iterative updates to radical, quality-of-life transformations. If your current e-reader is more than three or four years old, you are missing out on significant upgrades in display tech, ecosystem independence, and everyday responsiveness.

XTEINK X4 Classic

The XTEINK X4 Classic (also known as the X4 V2) is an ultra-thin, pocket-sized E-Ink eReader designed to snap onto the back of a smartphone or slip effortlessly into a pocket. Released in September 2026, it serves as the direct successor to the original X4 (which has been discontinued) and refines the “pure” tiny reader concept by prioritizing physical controls and extreme portability over touchscreens

XTEINK X4 Classic Pocket eReader, Ultra-Light 68g & 4.9mm Thin, Space Black

  • Ultra-Light, Ultra-Thin & Magnetic-Ready: Weighing just 2.4 oz and measuring only 0.19" thin, the compact design fits comfortably in one hand and slips easily into a pocket or bag. Magnetic-ready for quick attachment—reading begins the moment you flip.
  • Dual Page-Turn & Flexible Book Transfer: Choose physical buttons or shake-to-turn for convenient one-handed reading. Easily transfer and convert books or comics via XTEINK App transfer, microSD Card or USB, with support for TXT, EPUB, MOBI, PDF and PNG formats. Data is processed locally.

The Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (12th Generation) is the standard-bearer for mid-range eReaders, built for seamless access to the vast Amazon Kindle Store. Designed as a larger, more premium alternative to the entry-level Kindle Basic, the current iteration features a 7-inch flush-front display

entries.title: eBooks.com has launched two new reading apps for iOS and Android
entries.summary: The new reading apps are now available for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. They seamlessly support a wide range of ebook formats, including fixed-format EPUB, audio-visual content, manga, and textbooks with complex layouts and specialized fonts. The post eBooks.com has launched two new reading apps for iOS and Android first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
eBooks.com has launched completely new iOS and Android reading apps, developed through an Australian-European partnership. The launch forms part of a wider renewal of our reading platform, including Readium LCP, our new Online Reader, and support for Thorium.

The new reading apps are now available for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. They seamlessly support a wide range of ebook formats, including fixed-format EPUB, audio-visual content, manga, and textbooks with complex layouts and specialized fonts.

Developed in partnership with the European Digital Reading Lab and Sweden’s Colibrio, the new apps provide a simpler, faster, and more accessible reading experience, with support for offline reading, extensive typography and display controls, and modern accessibility features.

The apps form part of eBooks.com’s transition to open, standards-based reading technologies, including Readium LCP. They follow the company’s recent introduction of a new browser-based Online Reader and its support for the Thorium desktop reading application.

eBooks.com’s founder, Stephen Cole, said, “Our new reading platform is a delight to use. It’s bristling with useful features and is built with a clear focus on accessibility, simplicity and interoperability. It will support eBooks.com’s continued growth for years to come.

“I am especially proud of the apps’ attention to the needs of readers with disabilities. The new apps integrate with the assistive technologies built into iOS and Android, including VoiceOver and TalkBack. But they also provide extensive additional controls over typography and presentation. Readers can alter text size, typeface, spacing, alignment, colours, margins and other aspects of the page. We have also developed reading options intended to make ebooks more comfortable for people with dyslexia and other reading or visual preferences.”

entries.title: XTEINK says they will include USB-C ports on future devices
entries.summary: XTEINK has disclosed that future e-book readers will continue to use both pogo pins and USB-C for charging. The post XTEINK says they will include USB-C ports on future devices first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Xteink X4 Classic, X4 Pro, and X3 use pogo pins to charge. The company chose this charging method to keep its devices as thin and light as possible. However, there has been some serious backlash, since the popular X4 model had a USB-C port, which made charging super easy and put Xteink on the map.

Xteink currently offers no models with USB-C ports, and the anti-pogo complaints are becoming too loud to ignore. The company took to Reddit to solicit consumer feedback. They stated, “X4 Classic is a product where we wanted to keep pushing the physical form of the original X4: lighter, thinner, and closer to something that simply disappears into the things you already carry. For X4 Classic, we prioritized the device’s physical form over the convenience of a universal port.”

They went on to say, ” There are people who want the smallest, lightest reading device possible. And there are people who would happily accept a slightly thicker device in exchange for USB-C, a front light, touch, or other conveniences. We’ll keep exploring thinner and lighter e-Readers, while also working toward bringing USB-C back as an option in future products. That work has already started.”

It seems Xteink will focus on a few key areas. A feature-rich e-reader with a front light, touchscreen, a cheaper model, and a future device with a USB-C port to appeal to a wide array of users. Xteink has to listen to its users because they are a small company and has to cater to its fans. They certainly aren’t Amazon, where they can do whatever they want, and people will still buy them.

entries.title: Kobo fixes the e-book syncing problem
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo has rebuilt its e-reader and app syncing system for bookmarks and e-book progress. Here is how you can fix it on your devices. The post Kobo fixes the e-book syncing problem first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
In Kobo’s early days, they knew most people would buy one of their e-readers, buy books on them, and read. As the company matured, they released a series of new devices virtually every year and maintained a whole suite of mobile apps and a cloud reader. The syncing system was bursting at the seams, and new books and reading progress weren’t working properly.

Kobo CEO Michael Tambyn took to Bluesky to outline what they have done to solve the syncing issue. “We know some of you have been driven slowly crazy by the way your reading progress on the Kobo app doesn’t always correctly sync with your e-reader or your e-reader to your app. Annoying. Bad experience. No one liked it. So we rebuilt the entire bookmarking and progress syncing system from the ground up.”

He went on to say, “First off, this only matters if you are an e-reader and an app user. Or a multi-ereader user. If you aren’t trying to keep two devices in sync, this hasn’t been a problem for you. If you are using an e-reader, go into Settings > Device Information> Repair Your Kobo Account. Or, for apps, sign out of your account and then sign back in. You have to do this on all devices you’re signed in to, but you only have to do it once; after that, everything will stay synced from now on.”

entries.title: Flowtica Verso is an e INK AI screen that attaches to your phone
entries.summary: The Flowtica Verso's always-on e-paper (E-Ink) display sets it apart from standard, screenless AI voice recorders. The post Flowtica Verso is an e INK AI screen that attaches to your phone first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Flowtica Verso is an ultra-thin, magnetic AI voice recorder and productivity sidekick that features a built-in, always-on e-paper touchscreen. Announced by Flowtica at IFA 2026, the device is designed to act as a distraction-free “second surface” for your phone. Instead of forcing you to unlock your phone and dive into apps to read transcripts, the Verso displays meeting summaries, action items, calendars, and to-do lists directly on its own screen.

The Flowtica Verso is an ultra-thin, MagSafe-compatible AI voice recorder and productivity device machined from a single piece of aluminum-magnesium alloy. Weighing just 98 grams, it attaches magnetically to your smartphone to act as a distraction-free “second surface,” featuring an integrated, always-on e-paper touchscreen with a sharp 259 PPI resolution.

To capture meetings with high precision, it uses an advanced audio array of four MEMS microphones paired with a bone-conduction microphone, enabling it to isolate up to 15 different speakers from up to 5 meters away.

The device includes 64 GB of local storage and delivers an impressive 72 hours of battery life per charge via USB-C. For seamless connectivity, it includes Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and a built-in NFC digital business card for fast contact sharing. On the software side, it automatically transcribes multilingual audio into structured summaries and offers an interactive “Ask AI” voice search that lets you instantly query your meeting history, displaying answers right on its glare-free screen.

The device isn’t out yet, and the price hasn’t been officially disclosed. Visit their website to claim a 25% off perk by joining their mailing list and get informed on when it launches.

entries.title: How to read Kindle Books on a Dual Screen
entries.summary: Using the Amazon Kindle app on a book-style foldable phone delivers a near-physical book experience, offering a compact single-page view on the cover screen and an expansive two-page spread on the unfolded inner display. The post How to read Kindle Books on a Dual Screen first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon doesn’t make a dual-screen Kindle, but you can get two-column views on existing devices or consider alternative dual-screen e-readers. Devices like the dual-screen e-paper InkLeaf feature a book-like fold, enabling you to read on one display and take notes on the other.

The Kindle app on tablets like iPads supports a two-column layout via the Aa formatting menu under layout and columns. You can view two pages at once by opening a book on a Kindle Scribe, tapping the Aa menu, selecting the layout tab, and changing the orientation to landscape mode for a two-column display

Some people love reading books on their phone, since it is always in their pocket. However, the current generation of foldables lets you view two pages side by side when the phone is unfolded, providing a better reading experience, akin to reading a paperback or hardcover. The upcoming iPhone Duo will let you read Kindle books on a dual-screen OLED display that should increase text resolution. Previous-generation devices are also quite popular, such as the Google Pixel Fold. Samsung’s latest foldable models are the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 and the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra. However, foldable phones tend to be expensive, often costing over two thousand dollars.

I don’t think Amazon would make a dual-screen e-reader anytime soon. Flexible or dual-screen folding E-Ink panels are expensive, less durable, and harder to manufacture without a visible crease or hinge gap that disrupts text. tandard Kindles are prized for being ultra-lightweight and affordable. A foldable dual-screen design would dramatically increase the price and weight.

entries.title: Simon & Schuster is making indie publishing easier
entries.summary: I think these new imprints are great for people who want to slap a major publisher's logo on their physical or digital books, adding credibility to their content and helping it stand out from all the other AI slop. The post Simon & Schuster is making indie publishing easier first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Simon & Schuster has launched and repurposed specific imprints targeted at successful self-published and independent authors. These two new imprints combine digital-first initiatives with physical books. No agents are required for either initiative.

The publisher is relaunching Pocket Books, but this time they’re calling it a “Home for Self-Published Authors.” They have also launched Simon Stream, a hybrid indie digital imprint that works directly with authors to publish or republish books or series. Though Simon Stream doesn’t offer advances, it provides editing, formatting, and professional covers to help books it believes in “go as far as possible.”

Pocket Books is a reimagined imprint that will not release books in the old mass-market format, but will instead focus on signing self-published authors to print deals. The new mission is to rebrand Pocket “as a home for forward-thinking writers, including bestselling indie and hybrid authors looking to amplify their reach” using S&S’s strengths in marketing, publicity, and print distribution.

Simon & Schuster UK and International has launched Simon Stream, a digital-focused fiction imprint for self-published authors who want to switch to traditional publishing. Simon Stream aims to offer authors “the best parts of both [self- and traditional] publishing models,” with a focus on royalty rates. Simon Stream offers 50% net royalties on e-book sales, while a typical e-book royalty rate for traditional publishers hovers around 25%.

I think these new imprints are great for people who want to slap a major publisher’s logo on their physical or digital books, which adds credibility to their content and helps it stand out from all the other AI slop.

entries.title: US e-book sales decline slightly in June 2026
entries.summary: Digital book revenues were down 0.3% to $86.4 million in June, while digital audiobook revenues were up 3.9% to $97.4 million. The post US e-book sales decline slightly in June 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Digital book revenues were down 0.3% to $86.4 million in June, while digital audiobook revenues were up 3.9% to $97.4 million. Physical Audio revenues were down 30.1% to $500 thousand. Year-to-date e-book revenues were down 3.0% compared to 2025, totaling $516.1 million. Digital Audiobook revenue was up 12.6% to $597.8 million, while Physical Audio revenue was down 12.3% to $2.7 million.

Digital audiobooks are officially outselling e-books in traditional publishing, driven by double-digit revenue growth and rising consumer demand for multitasking formats. Audiobooks command over 11% of the total book market, edging ahead of e-books.

The Audio Publishers Association 2026 Consumer Survey, conducted by Edison Research at SSRS, adds that 63% of audiobook listeners listened in the last year and 35% in the last month. Audiobook Listeners averaged 3.8 audiobooks in the last year, and 26% listened to four or more titles in the last year.

Audiobook listening occurs across various platforms. Among those who listened in the last year, many used multiple sources: 49% purchased directly from websites/apps, 48% listened via a subscription service, 46% borrowed through a digital library app, and 42% used credits from a dedicated audiobook service.

entries.title: Is the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition Discontinued?
entries.summary: The Amazon Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition appears to be discontinued in the United States and many other countries. Does this mean a new model is coming? The post Is the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition Discontinued? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon might have discontinued the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition in the United States and other international markets such as the United Kingdom. This was the first color e-reader Amazon released and suffered from a yellow banding issue that persisted for nearly a year before it was finally resolved. Will this potential discontinuation make way for a new Kindle model coming out later this year?

Amazon’s main U.S. website says the Kindle Colorsoft SE is currently unavailable, and the same applies across multiple Amazon properties. Amazon commands an estimated 72% to 75% market share of e-reader devices and roughly 67% to 83% of e-book sales in the United States. However, it is still available in some countries, such as Canada, where Amazon controls less than 30% of the market because Kobo controls that market.

Amazon announced the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition on October 16, 2024, and it officially shipped on October 30, 2024. Amazon chose to move forward with a color Kindle because it saw an opportunity to build a better color filter with E Ink and rebuild the display stack to support it. In other words, Amazon decided to forgo Gallery 3 and do things differently. “Everything we do is customized. None of it is off the shelf. It’s all customized by our display engineers, and every level of the stack is created by our team,” said Keith. Kindle Colorsoft comes with wireless charging, up to eight weeks of battery life, and is waterproof, so you can take it into the bath or to the beach without worry.

Although the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition appears to be sold out, the company is still selling the Kindle Colorsoft 16GB version. Amazon finally addressed this issue by updating the screen assembly and motherboard. The Kindle Colorsoft 16GB was the first new e-reader with all these fixes, making e-book reading more enjoyable. The background is as grey as a Paperwhite, and the fonts are deeper and blacker.

Will Amazon just continue to sell the Kindle Colorsoft 16GB and discontinue the Signature Edition? Or do you think they’ll release a new premium model?

entries.title: Bigme B6 Pro Color Review
entries.summary: The Bigme B6 Pro is a compact 6-inch e-reader powered by Android 14, offering full access to the Google Play Store, a sharp display, and expandable storage. The post Bigme B6 Pro Color Review first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Bigme B6 Pro Color is a premium, pocket-sized 6-inch color E-Ink e-reader and paper tablet. Released globally as a major upgrade over standard compact e-readers, it blends a retro, blocky design with advanced internal hardware and unprecedented refresh speed. It runs an older version of Android 14, but you can install apps via Google Play.

Hardware

The Bigme B6 Pro features a 6-inch Kaleido 3 color e-paper screen, presenting crisp monochrome text at 300 PPI and color content at 150 PPI. Boasts an industry-leading refresh rate of 75-85 FPS, drastically minimizing ghosting and enabling incredibly smooth web browsing, comic panning, and video playback.

The Bigme B6 Pro features a highly customizable 36-level adjustable dual front-light system. It uses white and amber LEDs on the side bezels to direct light across the screen, providing glare-free, paper-like illumination that emits zero blue light and remains flicker-free.

Under the hood is a MediaTek Dimensity 1080 processor, 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of internal storage. It also has a MicroSD card slot that supports up to 1 TB of additional storage. It supports dual-band Wi-Fi (2.4GHz / 5GHz) and Bluetooth 5.1. Built-in high-definition Hi-Fi stereo speaker and dual-microphone array with integrated GPT AI voice transcription. It is powered by a 2,100 mAh battery.

Supports an active capacitive pen that charges via USB for handwriting, sketch note-taking, and PDF document markup. Built-in local GPT artificial intelligence models capable of real-time multi-language voice transcription, text generation, document translation, and one-click meeting summaries. Bigme uses something proprietary with this pen; we tried 15 different pens, and nothing else worked on the screen.

Software

The Bigme B6 Pro runs on Android 14 and provides full access to the Google Play Store, letting users install third-party applications like Kindle, Chrome, and Moon Reader Pro. As noted in reviews from eWritable and TechRadar, the software interface includes custom speed and refresh rate profiles—such as a high-refresh Hyper mode—to optimize e-ink performance for different tasks like reading or web browsing.

Despite Android 14’s flexibility, reviewers note that the native skin and built-in reading tools feel unpolished and unfinished out of the box. Users on platforms like Reddit generally agree that the software experience improves significantly once you bypass the default reading app and configure third-party alternatives. The system also features a customizable capacitive touch strip at the bottom of the screen that can be mapped to shortcuts or navigation commands.

Overall, the software bridges the gap between a traditional e-reader and a mini Android tablet, though it requires some personal setup to shine. While the inclusion of advanced e-ink center controls and AI features adds functional depth, some users find the stock software ecosystem cluttered compared to simpler dedicated readers.

Reading

With a 6-inch 300 PPI E Ink display and 150 PPI for Colour content, this is a great e-reader. It includes a stock reading app that works well for sideloaded content. It supports all major formats, so you can quickly load your collection of e-books, PDFs, manga, or other digital content. The default reading app offers a range of functionality, including font size, Typesetting, Text Contrast, and Picture Contrast. The latter two create an interesting scenario, as the device treats the two elements differently and lets you set text and picture contrast independently. The device also lets you change settings and view the effects live in the background. It’s like sliding the Font Size option to its maximum position and seeing the change take effect on the page in the background.

PDF files look simply fabulous. Quality and speed are top-notch, with pages turning extremely fast. Note-taking is instantaneous, with almost zero latency. Also, since it runs Android, complete with Play Store support, you can install any PDF reader you prefer. That said, the stock software that comes with the PocketNote 2 Color does a great job, and you are unlikely to encounter any issues with it reading PDF files.

Wrap Up

The Bigme B6 Pro Color is a compact 6-inch e-reader powered by Android 14, with full access to the Google Play Store, a sharp display, and expandable storage. While it offers a versatile alternative to traditional dedicated e-readers by breaking free from single-store ecosystems, its heavy OS results in a less polished interface and shorter battery life.

The included stylus for the Bigme B6 Pro Color receives widespread criticism for its awkward size, poor pressure sensitivity, and lack of functional shortcuts. The pen has a small, slippery, and awkward shape that doesn’t dock inside the device body and cannot magnetically snap to the side. While it features a USB Type-C charging port and a tip-removal clip, carrying it relies on an awkward dangling magnetic case loop. The redesigned stylus lacks a physical eraser button or secondary shortcut key, forcing users to manually select on-screen tool options instead.
